name: Build & Converge
purpose: Execute one Core-selected ready Bolt at a time in isolated Git worktrees, collect verifier evidence, stop non-converging or out-of-contract work, and produce a pinned Runnable Candidate only after all Bolt and integration checks pass.
completion_criteria: Core selects exactly one ready Bolt from the approved Build Contract DAG; AI cannot choose the Bolt or Stage route.
Execute work occurs only in isolated Git worktrees rooted at the accepted source revisions, and changed paths stay within the selected Bolt targets.
Every attempt records immutable changed-file and verifier Evidence; a failed attempt retries the same Bolt and three identical failure signatures stop the Stage.
Core marks a Bolt complete only when its machine verifiers pass, then selects the next ready Bolt and runs the integration verifiers after all Bolts complete.
Core creates a canonical Runnable Candidate and Build Current only after all Bolt and integration checks pass, then advances only through the fixed ST-06 to ST-07 Graph edge.
A Build Contract Current with not_applicable deterministically records an ST-06 not_applicable Current without Git execution or a Runnable Candidate.
stop_conditions: The approved Build Contract, approval, System Map source snapshot, Effective Policy, Core Plan, State, session, request, checkpoint, verifier Evidence, or candidate is missing, malformed, stale, tampered, or inconsistent.
An execute source is not a Git Repository, its accepted revision is unavailable, its ordinary working tree is dirty, or its HEAD drifted from the accepted baseline before the session starts.
A changed path is outside the Core-selected Bolt targets, a verifier command differs from the approved argv/cwd, or an operation crosses a Repository boundary.
The same failure signature occurs three times, an approved policy budget is exhausted, a verifier times out, or the Build Contract contradicts observed source state.
A destructive or external operation, credential, merge conflict, base drift, or unsafe Git operation would require authority not granted by the approved Build Contract.
